Show More

The Show More component truncates long text to a fixed number of lines and appends a Show more / Show less button. No configuration beyond a line count is needed.

Basic Show More

Drop data-zak-showmore on any text element. The value is the number of lines to show before truncating.

ZAKUIKit is a design system that bundles a component library, utility tokens and guidance. It gives every team the same building blocks, so screens stay consistent no matter who builds them. The Show More pattern clips long paragraphs to a few lines and lets people expand the rest on demand, keeping product pages tidy. In this demo the text is truncated at three rendered lines, and clicking the generated button toggles the remaining content. You can control the threshold with the attribute value, from one line up to as many as you like.

HTML
<p data-zak-showmore="3">Long paragraph here...</p>

Adjusting the Line Count

Set the number of visible lines by changing the attribute; the button still appears only when the text actually overflows.

2 lines

Short previews help users scan a feed quickly. With two lines you show only the very start of the text, and the rest fades behind the toggle button. ZAKUIKit computes the truncation height from the measured line-height, so the behavior stays correct at any font size or density.

5 lines

Five lines reveal more context before the fold. Use a larger threshold for summaries where the first sentence matters. A single line hides almost everything; more lines keep the preview readable while still condensing the noise on long cards or comment threads.

HTML
<p data-zak-showmore="2">Preview at two lines</p>
<p data-zak-showmore="5">Preview at five lines</p>

No Truncation For Short Text

When the content fits within the limit, no button is appended and no clipping happens.

This single sentence is well under three lines, so nothing is clamped — the paragraph renders in full with no toggle below it.

HTML
<p data-zak-showmore="3">Short content — stays untouched.</p>

Global API & Events

Call zak.showMore.init() after injecting new markup. The component fires zak:open and zak:close events on the text element.

Listen for the events to trigger analytics or lazy-load content that only matters once the full text is visible. The full original text is also stored on the element as data-zak-showmore-full before truncation runs.

HTML
// Re-init after AJAX-injected content
zak.showMore.init();

// React to expand/collapse
document.querySelector('[data-zak-showmore]').addEventListener('zak:open', function () {
    console.log('expanded');
});

CSS Classes

HTML
/* Injected by zak.showMore.init() */
.zak-showmore-truncated      /* Applied once content overflows */
.zak-showmore-expanded       /* Applied while fully open */
.zak-showmore-btn            /* The generated toggle button */

JavaScript API

HTML
zak.showMore.init()          // Scans [data-zak-showmore] and binds buttons
zak.showMore._truncate(el, lines)  // (internal) clamp an element

Events on target element:
  zak:open     // content expanded
  zak:close    // content collapsed

Data attributes:
  data-zak-showmore          // number of visible lines (default 3)
  data-zak-showmore-full     // original full text (set by init)

Accessibility

  • The generated button is a real <button>, so it is focusable and works with Enter/Space.
  • The button sits directly after the text, so the expand action reads in document order.
  • Consider pairing the text with a visually-hidden count (e.g. “5 lines shown”) when the preview length matters.
  • For large content, native <details> or an Expandable Panel is often a better semantic fit.
  • Never rely on the clipping alone — the original text remains fully in the DOM and readable by assistive tech.
